PullRequest.Title: editor: adopt @vscode/diff 0.0.2-122
PullRequest.Body:
﻿Adopts `@vscode/diff` 0.0.2-122 for the `advanced-external` and `advanced-wasm` diff algorithms. Follow-up to [#344144](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344144).

## Changes
- **Bump `@vscode/diff` 0.0.2-7 → 0.0.2-122.** The new version:
  - reports wasm columns in UTF-16 code units, so highlights are correct for non-ASCII text ([microsoft/vscode-packages#389](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/389));
  - supports `maxComputationTimeMs` in wasm (0.0.2-7 panicked when measuring time);
  - always diffs whitespace and annotates leading/trailing whitespace changes instead of accepting `ignoreTrimWhitespace` ([microsoft/vscode-packages#390](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-packages/pull/390)).
- **Bridge (`externalLinesDiffComputer.ts`):**
  - "Ignore trim whitespace" now hides replacements annotated with `isTrimWhitespaceChange`. It replaces VS Code's own `isInTrimWhitespace` check, which implemented the same rule and is removed.
  - Forwards `maxComputationTimeMs`, resolving the TODO from [#344144](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/344144).
- **`diffEditor.diffAlgorithm`** gets `experiment: { mode: 'startup' }`, so an A/B experiment can assign `advanced-wasm`. `startup` so the algorithm doesn't switch under open diff editors.

The default (`advanced`) is unchanged, so this only affects users who opt in to `advanced-external` / `advanced-wasm` or are assigned by an experiment.

## Lockfile note
The `pnpm-lock.yaml` change is limited to `@vscode/diff` (5 lines). I generated it against the public npm registry, because the internal package feed proxy hadn't synced 0.0.2-122 yet. Resolution there also drifted `@playwright/cli` (`latest` specifier), which I dropped. The integrity hash matches the npm-published tarball, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` accepts the lockfile.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck-client` and eslint on the changed files: pass.
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/editor/test/node/diffing/fixtures.test.ts --run src/vs/editor/test/node/diffing/verifyLinesDiff.test.ts --run src/vs/editor/test/node/diffing/defaultLinesDiffComputer.test.ts`: 126 passing. This includes all diffing fixtures through `advanced-external` and `advanced-wasm`, with and without ignoring trim whitespace.
- `scripts\test.bat` with the same files: 126 passing.
- Code OSS with `"diffEditor.diffAlgorithm": "advanced-wasm"`, `"diffEditor.ignoreTrimWhitespace": true` and `"diffEditor.experimental.verifyDiffSampleRate": 1`, on a diff with emoji/CJK and on the [#333747](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333747) repro:
  - `diffEditor.computeDiff` reports `validity: valid`;
  - no wasm panic or assertion errors.

Related: [#318958](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/318958), [#317301](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/317301), [#333747](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333747)

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The external diff adapters ignored the caller's time budget and synchronously computed the full diff in the shared editor worker, allowing CPU work and awaited diff-render latency to grow without the configured 5-second bound.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Opening or updating a large/pathological diff with advanced-external or advanced-wasm could keep the editor worker occupied and delay diff rendering past diffEditor.maxComputationTime instead of quitting early.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The bridge now passes options.maxComputationTimeMs into @vscode/diff, so external JavaScript and WASM computations can terminate at the same configured budget as the built-in advanced algorithm and return a coarse timed-out result rather than running to completion.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base bridge explicitly omitted maxComputationTimeMs on the synchronous @vscode/diff computeDiff call (base line 59), while DiffEditorViewModel awaits WorkerBasedDocumentDiffProvider.computeDiff before committing/rendering the result, and the worker invokes diffAlgorithm.computeDiff synchronously. The UI option defaults to 5000 ms and is documented as cancelling computation after that budget, but advanced-external/advanced-wasm discarded it; large or pathological diffs could therefore keep the editor worker busy and leave the diff editor awaiting a result beyond the configured bound. Blame identifies cf676eb9119f308cb6337e778689af22a38152a2 as introducing the omitted-forwarding line.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or update a diff editor using advanced-external or advanced-wasm
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After debounced model changes, DiffEditorViewModel awaits WorkerBasedDocumentDiffProvider, which awaits editor-worker IPC and the synchronous external computeDiff result before committing the diff for rendering. The first request also awaits lazy module/computer creation; later requests reuse it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize the two text models to the editor worker and invoke $computeDiff, then deserialize line mappings on return.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One worker diff request per exact model-version/options cache miss; the view-model debounce coalesces bursts of edits and WorkerBasedDocumentDiffProvider reuses an exact cached result. The cache is capped around 10 URI pairs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same worker request and model synchronization occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The diff editor cannot publish/render the updated diff until this request returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Lazily import @vscode/diff and create the selected JavaScript or WASM computer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one module import shared by both modes and one computer-creation promise per useWasm boolean for the worker lifetime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior package version used the same lazy import and per-mode promise caches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only the cold first external diff waits for module/computer initialization; warm requests use cached promises.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU work scales with the two documents' length and diff complexity; adapter conversion scales with the number of replacements and moves. Effective boundary cardinality remains one worker request per uncached diff computation, not one per change.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The external computation is synchronous within the editor worker, so one computation occupies that worker event loop; initialization is coalesced by externalModulePromise and externalComputers. The diff view model debounces content changes, while cancellation is checked after the worker result.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold use imports the package and initializes the chosen computer. Warm use reuses both promises. Exact diff results are cached by URI pair plus model IDs, versions, and options; misses recompute, and the result cache is bounded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the old bridge omitted the caller's 5-second default budget on the synchronous worker computation, and the added line forwards it. This is recorded as a regression fix rather than a finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual savings depend on document complexity and how many users select or are assigned an external algorithm; the mechanism is certain even though worst-case runtime is not measured here.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The PR bounds previously unbounded external diff CPU/latency with maxComputationTimeMs and replaces per-replacement trim-whitespace text scans with package metadata.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve the new startup experiment for diffEditor.diffAlgorithm
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ConfigurationService processes experimental settings during updateDefaults and awaits the treatment lookup before reloading defaults; this occurs on startup. It does not import @vscode/diff or initialize WASM. External code is still loaded only when a diff actually uses that assigned algorithm.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the treatment for config.diffEditor.diffAlgorithm from the shared TAS client, preferring cached assignments while initial assignment fetching is pending.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional treatment-key lookup during startup processing. The TAS client and its initial assignments fetch are shared across the many existing experiment-backed settings, so this declaration does not establish an additional network request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This setting had no treatment lookup, although startup already initialized the shared assignment client and resolved many other experiment-backed settings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The lookup is awaited by experimental-default processing, but normally reads from the shared client/cache; no external diff module work is placed on startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant one added experiment-key lookup per startup, independent of files, editors, or document size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Experimental settings are iterated with awaited lookups; assignment data comes from one shared TAS client whose initial fetch is reused, rather than a per-setting network call.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Treatments use the shared TAS client's persisted/current assignment state. Startup-mode values are latched once resolved; unresolved values may be retried on a shared assignment refetch.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that one lookup is introduced and that heavyweight diff initialization remains lazy; low evidence of any measurable startup degradation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository code does not quantify the in-memory treatment lookup duration, but it does show no per-setting network fan-out and no eager diff/WASM initialization.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added experiment eligibility introduces only a shared-client treatment lookup, not a new network fetch or eager diff-engine startup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Filter trim-whitespace replacements returned by the external diff engine
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After external computeDiff returns, the adapter walks every replacement before constructing line mappings and returning through worker IPC.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Adapter CPU scales with replacement count. Before the PR each replacement under ignoreTrimWhitespace could run regexes, substring allocation, and line-boundary searches; after the PR it checks the replacement's isTrimWhitespaceChange metadata.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Runs synchronously as part of the single worker computation; there is no fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No separate cache applies inside this conversion; the enclosing exact diff-result cache can avoid the entire computation on a repeated identical request.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High from the deleted helper and added metadata predicate.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number and size of replacements vary by diff, but the changed operation strictly removes text scanning/allocation from this loop.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. This is a per-replacement CPU/allocation reduction.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all four changed files and complete diff pages. No diff-introduced performance finding met the reporting threshold. Recorded the concrete regression fix that restores external diff time-budget enforcement; experiment lookup and package adoption add no proven boundary fan-out or eager startup work.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
